question: A 59-year-old woman with a personal history of breast cancer operated on 8 months ago and osteoporosis, suffers a fall and has a fracture of the right femur neck. She is operated on surgically and remains in bed with plaster for 10 days. A week after her high note suddenly a shortness of breath that leads her to consult her GP who notes that her right calf has edema and pain on palpation. What clinical elements would NOT be important in determining that you have a high clinical risk of pulmonary thromboembolism ?:

options.opc: The antecedent of having been more than 3 days at rest.
options.opd: The presence of unilateral edema of the right calf.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fracture of the right femur neck" -> "Surgical intervention" -> "Bed rest with plaster for 10 days" -> "Increased risk of venous stasis" -> "Possible development of deep vein thrombosis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Shortness of breath" -> "Right calf edema and pain on palpation" -> "Possible signs of deep vein thrombosis" -> "Increased suspicion for pulmonary thromboembolism" -> 85% CHAIN: "History of breast cancer" -> "Increased risk of hypercoagulability" -> "Potential predisposition to thromboembolic events" -> "Relevant for assessing pulmonary thromboembolism risk" -> 90% CHAIN: "History of osteoporosis" -> "Not directly related to pulmonary thromboembolism risk" -> "Less important in determining high clinical risk of pulmonary thromboembolism" -> 70% CHAIN: "Being more than 3 days at rest" -> "Increased risk of venous stasis" -> "Possible predisposing factor for deep vein thrombosis" -> "Relevant for assessing pulmonary thromboembolism risk" -> 80% CHAIN: "Unilateral edema of the right calf" -> "Possible sign of deep vein thrombosis" -> "Indicates venous thromboembolism may be present" -> "Important in determining high clinical risk of pulmonary thromboembolism" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The history of breast cancer and being more than 3 days at rest are important clinical elements in determining a high clinical risk of pulmonary thromboembolism. The history of osteoporosis and the presence of unilateral edema of the right calf are less crucial in this context.
analysis: The core medical principle in this scenario is the identification of clinical elements that increase the risk of pulmonary thromboembolism. The history of breast cancer and prolonged immobilization are well-established risk factors for thromboembolism. Osteoporosis, although a risk factor for fractures, is not a direct contributor to thromboembolism. Unilateral edema of the right calf, known as deep vein thrombosis (DVT), is a significant clinical sign of potential thromboembolism. Therefore, the presence of unilateral edema of the right calf would be important in determining a high clinical risk of pulmonary thromboembolism.
